name: Harhaiah
overview: Harhaiah is a male biblical figure known primarily as a goldsmith and the father of Uzziel. The Scriptures identify him specifically in Nehemiah 3:8, highlighting his role within the community during the post-exilic period. No additional tribal affiliation or personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Harhaiah appears once in Scripture without a provided meaning or special title. It is simply presented as a proper name in Nehemiah 3:8.
familyAndRelationships: Harhaiah is noted as the father of Uzziel, an inferred relationship based on the biblical text in Nehemiah 3:8. Beyond this paternal connection, Scripture does not record other family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Harhaiah's significance lies in his identification as a goldsmith involved in the rebuilding efforts described in Nehemiah 3:8. His mention underscores the contribution of skilled craftsmen and their families in the restoration of Jerusalem's walls, reflecting the communal dedication to God's work during this period. As the father of Uzziel, Harhaiah is connected to a lineage contributing to the physical and spiritual renewal of the people.
